verdict_reason: Fixtures and cookie-aware request helpers are sound and cookieHeaderOf is correctly promoted, but the default create matcher's name hides its addressType guard and the testing.md catalogue misses VALID_ADDRESS_RECORD and the default matcher.

todos.issue: carriesRoles (address-book-requests.js:105-106) returns true only when the body has roles AND has no addressType key; the name predicts the first check and hides the second, which is the guard that the add controller strips the form-only addressType before calling the API, so serveAddressCreated()'s default matcher refuses a body a reader would expect it to accept.
todos.fix: Must: the default create-body matcher's name states both conditions it checks (roles present, no addressType). One way: rename to carriesRolesWithoutAddressType, or split into two named predicates combined in serveAddressCreated's default.

todos.issue: The helper catalogue in src/server/app/docs/testing.md:55-81 lists VALID_ADDRESS_FIELDS and VALID_ADDRESS_PAYLOAD but not the new VALID_ADDRESS_RECORD (address-book-requests.js:85, used by address-book.test.js and address-book.roles.test.js), and describes serveAddressCreated(matchBody) (testing.md:75) without its new default matcher (line 108), so a test author reading the catalogue rebuilds the API-shaped record locally or passes a matcher that is now redundant.
todos.fix: Must: testing.md's address-book-requests entry names every exported fixture, including VALID_ADDRESS_RECORD (the fields with the stored roles array, as the API takes them), and says what serveAddressCreated matches when called with no matcher. One way: add both to the fixtures and stubs lists in the same paragraph.
